question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool scheduling mode in agent-core, and should early execution require explicit concurrency-safe tool metadata before any tool can start during streaming?
rationale: The source-level latency gap is clear, but the fix changes core runtime semantics and safety policy rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open for an owner design covering streaming dispatch, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, config/API exposure, and regression proof.

options.title: Block On Tool Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat this as dependent on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract before implementing early execution.

options.title: Decline Early Execution
options.body: Keep the current post-stream parallel batching model if maintainers decide the safety and transcript complexity outweighs the latency win.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for an owner design covering streaming dispatch, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, config/API exposure, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across agent-core, provider stream, and MCP/tool parallelism surfaces involved in the product decision.
